questions.stem: A 42-year-old man comes to the physician because of bright red blood in his stool for 5 days. He has had no pain during defecation and no abdominal pain. One year ago, he was diagnosed with liver cirrhosis after being admitted to the emergency department for upper gastrointestinal bleeding. He has since reduced his drinking and consumes around 2 bottles of beer daily. Examination shows scleral icterus and mild ankle swelling. Palpation of the abdomen shows a fluid thrill. Anoscopy shows enlarged bluish vessels above the dentate line. Which of the following is this patient's most likely source of bleeding?
